Figure 1:Coefficients of the cells of the length and position grid by text length slice before the
shift correction. The points of one slice are connected by a line; the dashed line is the hyperbola
of the slice with the shared parametersκS\kappa_{S},λS\lambda_{S},ωS\omega_{S}and its own plateau levelμv\mu_{v}. Whiskers are the 95% confidence interval of the coefficient of a cell.

Figure 2:Plateau levels of the slicesμv\mu_{v}before the shift correction and the hyperbola of the
plateau law. The point of a slice stands at the mean length of its texts; whiskers are the 95%
confidence interval of the plateau level.

Figure 3:Coefficients of the cells of the length and position grid after the shift correction:δV​S=μ0\delta_{VS}=\mu_{0}is subtracted from all cells. The notation is the same as in
Figure1.

Figure 4:Plateau levels of the slices after the shift correction: the hyperbola of the plateau law
tends to zero for short texts. The notation is the same as in Figure2.

Figure 5:Coefficients of the replacement density bins and the density law before the shift
correction. The open marker is the bin on which the fit pinned the arbitrary constant; the dashed
line is the level of the shiftδP=μP\delta_{P}=\mu_{P}. Whiskers are the 95% confidence interval of the
coefficient of a bin.

Figure 6:Replacement density bins and the density law after the shift correction:δP=μP\delta_{P}=\mu_{P}is subtracted from all bins. The notation is the same as in
Figure5.

Figure7.
